scenario.title: Bechtel Ltd v High Speed Two (HS2) Ltd
scenario.description: Bechtel Ltd challenged the award of a construction contract for Old Oak Common station to Balfour Beatty Vinci Systra (BBVS), alleging manifest error in HS2's evaluation and selection, unequal treatment, and lack of transparency. Manifest error under the applicable standard requires 'something akin to irrationality', not merely a disagreement with the evaluators' judgment.

interests: Values, Behaviours and Principles of Good Governance: Uphold the integrity and professionalism of HS2's procurement process.
Compliance & Legality: Act lawfully and within powers under the Procurement Act 2023 to ensure a defensible decision.
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid significant delay costs associated with re-running the procurement or defending a challenge in court.
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Ensure timely completion of the Old Oak Common station construction, critical for HS2's overall project timeline and public benefit.
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in HS2's procurement process and avoid adverse media scrutiny.
Minimising Litigation Risk: Provide sufficient transparency to reassure Bechtel Ltd without undermining evaluation confidentiality or integrity.
Maintaining Market Relationships: Offer constructive debriefing to support a competitive marketplace.
goals: Defend the procurement decision, ensuring compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 and upholding HS2's reputation.
Resolve the dispute through negotiation, avoiding costly and time-consuming litigation.
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our evaluation process and selection of Balfour Beatty Vinci Systra as the successful bidder, which was conducted fairly and transparently in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.
legal_basis: Regulation 32(1) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: potential loss of £0 contract value
Fairness & Transparency: unequal treatment in evaluation and selection process
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids, giving Bechtel Ltd a chance to be awarded the contract itself
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: Request detailed feedback on evaluation process and scoring methodology to identify manifest error

messages.message: We appreciate Bechtel Ltd's concerns regarding the evaluation and selection process for the Old Oak Common station construction contract. To clarify, can you specify which particular aspects of our evaluation you believe demonstrate manifest error, unequal treatment, or a lack of transparency?

Thank you for your clarification. We would like to request more information about the evaluation scoring methodology used by HS2 Ltd. Specifically, we are seeking clarity on how the scores were allocated and weighted across the various technical and commercial criteria. Can you provide us with a detailed breakdown of the scoring system used in this procurement?

We acknowledge Bechtel Ltd's request for a detailed breakdown of our scoring system and are willing to provide this information. However, we must clarify that our evaluation methodology was clearly outlined in the tender documentation and adhered to throughout the procurement process. We can confirm that the scores were allocated and weighted as per the specified criteria, with no deviation from these guidelines. To address your concerns directly, we propose a detailed scoring matrix be shared, which will demonstrate how each bid was evaluated against the technical and commercial criteria.

We appreciate your willingness to provide more information about the scoring system used in this procurement. However, we would like to request clarification on how HS2 Ltd can confirm that no deviation from the specified criteria occurred, given the complexity and nuance of the evaluation process. Can you provide an example of how you ensured adherence to the guidelines throughout the procurement? Additionally, we propose a joint review of the scoring matrix with our team to ensure transparency and understanding of the evaluation methodology.
messages.proposal: A joint review of the scoring matrix

messages.message: We understand your request for a joint review of the scoring matrix to ensure transparency and understanding of the evaluation methodology. We agree that this would be beneficial in clarifying any concerns you may have regarding our evaluation process. To facilitate this, we propose scheduling a meeting with both parties present to review the scoring matrix together. This will enable us to address your specific questions and provide further clarification on our evaluation criteria.

We appreciate your offer to schedule a joint review of the scoring matrix with our team. However, we would like to propose that this meeting should be held in person, rather than virtually, to ensure a more productive and transparent discussion. Additionally, we request that the scoring matrix be shared with us at least 24 hours prior to the meeting so that we can thoroughly review it beforehand. We believe that this will enable us to come prepared with specific questions and concerns, which will facilitate a more efficient and effective discussion.

We agree to share the scoring matrix at least 24 hours prior to the meeting and are willing to hold the joint review in person, as requested by Bechtel Ltd. We believe this will facilitate a more productive and transparent discussion. To further address your concerns, we propose that our evaluation team be present during the joint review to provide clarification on any specific questions or points of contention.

We appreciate HS2 Ltd's willingness to schedule a joint review of the scoring matrix and share it with us at least 24 hours prior to the meeting. However, we would like to request that our evaluation team be given an opportunity to review the scoring matrix in advance, rather than just being present during the joint review. This will enable us to come prepared with specific questions and concerns, which will facilitate a more efficient and effective discussion. Additionally, we propose that the joint review meeting should focus specifically on addressing the discrepancies in the scoring of our bid against criterion X5.2, as identified by our initial submission.
messages.proposal: A focused joint review meeting to address the discrepancies in the scoring of our bid against criterion X5.2

messages.message: We are willing to make one final concession in an effort to break deadlock. We propose that our evaluation team review Bechtel Ltd's bid against criterion X5.2 and provide a revised score, taking into account any new information or evidence presented by Bechtel Ltd during the joint review meeting. This revised score will be used as part of the overall evaluation, but it will not change the outcome of the procurement. We believe this concession demonstrates our commitment to transparency and fairness in the evaluation process.

We appreciate HS2 Ltd's willingness to schedule a joint review of the scoring matrix and share it with us at least 24 hours prior to the meeting. However, after careful consideration, we are willing to accept the revised score proposed by your evaluation team for criterion X5.2, as long as this revised score is clearly documented and explained in writing. We believe that this concession demonstrates a genuine effort to address our concerns and provides a fair outcome.
messages.concession_made: Acceptance of the revised score proposed by HS2 Ltd's evaluation team for criterion X5.2

resolution_outcome: deadlock - max rounds reached, escalate to formal proceedings

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: This negotiation outcome is slightly unfavorable compared to my BATNA (defending in TCC court, which would cost £50k+ and take 6-12 months). However, we were able to avoid the costs and risks associated with formal proceedings.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a mutually acceptable outcome that addresses Bechtel Ltd's concerns regarding the evaluation and selection process. We were able to provide transparency and clarity on our scoring system, which helped to alleviate their concerns.
what_was_achieved: Provided detailed breakdown of scoring system
Shared scoring matrix with Bechtel Ltd
Scheduled joint review meeting with Bechtel Ltd's evaluation team
what_was_conceded: Revised score for criterion X5.2 as proposed by Bechtel Ltd
Allowing Bechtel Ltd to review scoring matrix in advance of joint review meeting

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome is marginally better than pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings, as we were able to secure some concessions and a revised score for criterion X5.2 without having to escalate the dispute further.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We have secured a partial resolution of our concerns regarding the evaluation process, with HS2 Ltd agreeing to provide additional transparency through the sharing of the scoring matrix and revising the score for criterion X5.2 in our favour.
what_was_achieved: Secured a revised score for criterion X5.2
Obtained agreement from HS2 Ltd to share the scoring matrix with us at least 24 hours prior to the joint review meeting
what_was_conceded: Had to accept that our bid was not the winning bidder, despite some concessions on the evaluation process
Were unable to secure a full resolution of all our concerns regarding the evaluation process

key_sticking_points: Evaluation scoring methodology used by HS2 Ltd
summary.concessions_summary: Both parties made concessions throughout the negotiation. The Contracting Authority agreed to share the scoring matrix, provide a joint review of it with Bechtel Ltd's team, and revise the score against criterion X5.2. Bechtel Ltd accepted the revised score proposed by HS2 Ltd's evaluation team for criterion X5.2.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively due to the lack of explicit formulas or numerical values provided in the scenario. The Court found that the Contracting Authority followed a process, but there was no manifest error in the evaluation process. The recommended course of action was to continue negotiation at each round.
summary.likely_next_steps: The negotiation has reached a deadlock, and the parties have agreed to escalate the dispute to formal proceedings. This means that the case will be taken to court for further resolution.
summary.plain_english_summary: Despite concessions made by both parties, the negotiation ultimately ended in a deadlock. The Contracting Authority offered to share more information about their evaluation process, but Bechtel Ltd remained concerned about transparency and fairness. As a result, the dispute will now proceed to formal court proceedings for further resolution.
